items.title: Capsizings Cause the Deaths of 12 Migrants off Greek Islands
items.summary_raw:
ATHENS, Greece (AP) — A dozen migrants died in separate speedboat capsizings off the Greek islands of Lesbos and Samos, Greece's coast guard said Monday. An infant was among the dead. Six people died when a speedboat ferrying Syrian and Palestinian migrants struck the port side of a Greek coast guard vessel with its bow and capsized south of Lesbos late Sunday, a coast guard spokesperson told The Associated Press on customary condition of anonymity. Four men, one woman and an infant were among the dead. Another eight people, including an individual who has been detained as the suspected people smuggler, were rescued.

The post Capsizings Cause the Deaths of 12 Migrants off Greek Islands appeared first on The National Herald.

items.summary_raw:

  • Cop17 at a glance: everything you need to know about the UN’s nature summit

Passersby could smell the dead fish before they saw them. In August, more than 3,000 pike, roach, carp and rudd were found lifeless along the River Wensum in Norwich. Some gasped for air in their final moments, desperate for the oxygen that heatwave conditions had depleted in the water. Investigators believe that the die-off was triggered by heavy rainfall that flushed through high concentrations of pollution at a time when wildlife were already struggling.

The 45-mile (70km) chalk river is one of about 250 in the country. They are a geological accident almost unique to Britain – and one of Earth’s rarest habitats. items.title: Approximate flight routes of the missiles used in tonight's large-scale Russian combined attack on Kyiv Oblast.  The following was launched:  ~8 RM-48U modified S-400 ballistic mis…
items.summary_raw: Approximate flight routes of the missiles used in tonight's large-scale Russian combined attack on Kyiv Oblast.  The following was launched:  ~8 RM-48U modified S-400 ballistic missiles from near Klintsy, Bryansk Oblast.  ~7 Iskander-M ballistic missiles from near Klintsy and Pochep, Bryansk Oblast.  ~6 Iskander-K cruise missiles from near Fatezh, Kursk Oblast.  ~21 missiles in total.  Of these 21 missiles, 3 Iskander-K cruise missiles were shot down. None of the ballistic missiles were intercepted due to Ukraine having effectively run out of Patriot PAC-3 interceptors, although 6 out of 8 of the RM-48U missiles missed their target due to their low accuracy.  The following was struck:  - CHP-4 Combined Heat and Power Plant in eastern Kyiv by ~2 RM-48U S-400s.  - "Western" 330 kV electrical substation west of Kyiv by ~2 Iskander-Ms and ~3 Iskander-Ks.  - Unknown (probably industrial) target in western Kyiv by ~5 Iskander-Ms.  - 6 of the RM-48U missiles seemingly missed their target and fell in areas surrounding the CHP-4 Power Plant in eastern Kyiv.

items.summary_raw:
This month’s biodiversity summit in Yerevan, Armenia, aims to push governments to meet the 23 targets agreed at Cop15 in 2022

This month, nearly every country on Earth will return to the question of how to stem the rapid destruction of the natural world. Humans are driving it, but so far we have not found a way to stop it.

In late 2022, governments reached an ambitious once-in-a-decade deal to better protect nature amid scientific warnings that the planet is going through the largest loss of life since the extinction of the dinosaurs. Now, they are assessing their progress on the targets for the first time.

"It's not going to happen with those who want to accommodate and appease these tyrants," he said.

items.title: EPA quietly backtracks on claims US has phased out toxic Pfas compounds
items.summary_raw:
Agency changes wording on website as Texas-based firm continues manufacture of plastic container barriers

The Environmental Protection Agency has quietly backtracked on a claim that the US has phased out two of the most dangerous Pfas compounds – Pfoa and Pfos.

The EPA has found that virtually no level of exposure to either in drinking water is safe, and the International Agency for Research on Cancer classifies Pfoa as “carcinogenic to humans” and Pfos as “possibly carcinogenic”. Still, the EPA is allowing Houston-based Inhance to produce containers from which Pfoa has been found to leach at high levels into the containers’ contents. The company makes up to 200m barriers annually for plastic containers use

According to local sources on base, Canadian Forces personnel had been conducting exercises over several days when an artillery projectile reportedly struck an active natural gas well on the bombing range, triggering a massive detonation.  The blast is said to have levelled nearby tactical training buildings, with subsequent fires reaching munitions storage and setting off secondary detonations across the range. items.summary_raw: A wave of cost-of-living, education and housing protests swept across Europe, with France at the center and violent clashes in several cities.  🇫🇷 France: About 550,000 marched nationwide; Limoges town hall and a Lyon tourist office were set on fire, around 1,800 people were arrested and about 150 police officers injured.  🇧🇪 Belgium: Student-led protests in Brussels and Liège turned violent, with police using tear gas and water cannons and making about 45 arrests in Liège.  🇮🇹 Italy: About 100,000 marched peacefully in Rome, while clashes near Milan’s Duomo led to around 50 detentions.  🇵🇹 Portugal: Tens of thousands protested the housing crisis and low wages, with demonstrators camping overnight in Lisbon.  🇦🇱 Albania: Student-led protests demanding Prime Minister Edi Rama’s resignation entered a fifth day, with hundreds detained and more than 120 police injured.  🇪🇸 Spain: An ongoing housing movement has drawn mass marches and protest camps, contributing to the snap election set for November 29. Major US firms and trade associations, including Cargill, Bunge, Mondelēz and the US Soybean Export Council, as well as numerous other US firms and organizations, sought to influence the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) in more than 350 meetings, the advocacy group found.

Pakistan's finance minister said on Saturday the country had so far withstood the shock from skyrocketing energy prices due to the Iran war, but that attacks on infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and other Gulf countries were "worrying" for the country's longer-term economic outlook.

In an interview on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Muhammad Aurangzeb told AFP said the South Asian country had procured enough energy supplies to last through November, and was now planning for the winter months, when household needs typically spike.

The Pentagon says claims of munitions shortages are “false.”  The warning was a risk analysis in the Pentagon’s Global Force Management Allocation Plan for fiscal 2027, which sets where troops and weapons go worldwide, the officials said. They said THAAD and Patriot interceptors would stay strategically low, citing Patriot transfers to Ukraine, munitions used to defend Israel during the 12 Day War and reduced industrial capacity. CBS withheld the exact percentages for security reasons. Gen. George declined to comment.  Officials told CBS the U.S. still holds a significant stock of offensive munitions, such as JDAMs and Small Diameter Bombs, but missile defense interceptors are low. One said even with no further use, restoring the already low December 2025 levels would take until 2030. items.title: Josh Huck Officially Assumes Duties as Chargé d’Affaires ad Interim of the U.S. Diplomatic Mission to Greece
items.summary_raw:
ATHENS - Josh Huck officially assumed duties as Chargé d’Affaires ad interim, of the U.S. Diplomatic Mission to Greece, on Thursday October 15, 2026. A career member of the U.S. Foreign Service with the rank of Minister Counselor, Chargé d’Affaires Huck previously served as Deputy Chief of Mission at the U.S. Embassy in Athens. In his new capacity, he will lead the Mission’s continued efforts to advance U.S. priorities and further strengthen the longstanding strategic partnership between the United States and Greece. The United States remains firmly committed to its close partnership with Greece, including expanding defense and security cooperation, strengthening regional energy security, promoting trade and investment, and advancing shared interests in the Eastern Mediterranean and beyond.

Iguazu Falls, an Unesco world heritage site, has reached a record water flow after heavy rains across the river basin. El Niño weather patterns are said to have driven the water flow to hit 10 times the normal amount. Usually the water flow is 1.5m litres per second, but local government registered a flow of 15m litres of water per second.

items.title: Revealed: VW, Ford and Tesla batteries linked to destructive deforestation of indigenous lands
items.summary_raw:
Mines in supply chains of western carmakers linked to widespread deforestation of primary rainforest in nickel-rich lands inhabited by Tolaki people in Indonesia

Volkswagen, Ford and Tesla are among the electric carmakers whose batteries may contain nickel mined in indigenous woodlands plagued by deforestation, an analysis has found, highlighting the struggle to make vehicles that are free from environmental destruction.

Corporate disclosures and trade flows from the last two years show mines in the battery supply chains of automotive giants are linked to the loss of trees in Sulawesi, a wildlife hotspot in Indonesia that houses the world’s largest nickel deposits. The metal is widely used in cathodes in car batteries because it boosts energy density and increases range.

items.title: For the future of green politics, look beyond the Green party | Zoe Williams
items.summary_raw:
Environmentalists of all political hues must find the language and ideas that turn passion for climate action into impetus

The future of Green politics is under constant discussion after the Holborn and St Pancras byelection, but a much heavier clash – in meaning, symbolism and portent – happened earlier this summer, in King’s Lynn and West Norfolk. The council declared a climate emergency in 2021, along with hundreds of others, and while it was under Conservative control. It is now controlled by independents, and a Reform UK councillor, Austen Moore, moved to scrap the declaration.

It was the end of June, and the meeting had to be called off, because of the extreme heat in the King’s Lynn council chamber. A lot of people paused to grimly remark on that irony, but not Moore, who simply rescheduled the motion for the following week, where it was voted down (by 33 to seven). items.title: Mont Blanc, the ‘roof of Europe’, loses more than a metre of height in a year
items.summary_raw:
Peak of French mountain now 4,807 metres high and fluctuates year by year due to changes in Alpine climate

Western Europe’s highest mountain shrank by more than a metre last year. The peak of Mont Blanc in France now stands 4,807.47 metres above sea level, a team of surveyors said on Wednesday, putting “the roof of Europe” 1.29 metres lower than in 2025.

The mountain is about 4,792 metres tall but the summit constantly shifts as heat, wind and precipitation change the thickness of snow and ice on top. The height scientists recorded during an expedition last month was 1.88 metres greater than it was in 2023, when it reached the lowest levels in recent memory.

items.title: I work for a major insurer. Much of my industry is fudging the numbers in the face of the climate crisis | Anonymous
items.summary_raw:
Insurers are taking on more risk than they should. If – or when – a major disaster hits, the catastrophe will have far-reaching consequences

I work for a major insurer, assessing the risk posed by natural disasters on properties around the world, from family homes to schools, government offices and multibillion-dollar commercial centres. The world is facing greater risk than ever from extreme weather. We are not prepared – and that inaction could have profound consequences for the global financial system.

In the face of ever more extreme and unpredictable climate risks, I am coming under pressure to cut my forecasts for the losses that disasters will cause in order to make insurance more affordable – and get my employer more business. In some instances, the questioning of our numbers and models is justified. But too often, it is not being done to produce more accurate models, but to artificially lower prices. If this is happening at my firm, which is struggling to compete with rivals’ prices, it’s happening elsewhere.

The writer is a modeller working in the insurance industry. A version of this piece originally appeared with the Bureau of Investigative Journali

"CHELSEA 3" was reportedly hit by three different drones.   The Bulgarian Prime Minister has summoned Russian Ambassador Eleonora Mitrofanova, and is requesting urgent NATO surveillance over the area.

items.title: Trump says Iran wants deal with US but 'don’t know how to'
items.summary_raw:
Trump says Iran wants deal with US but 'don’t know how to'

US President Donald Trump says Iran wants to reach a deal with Washington, but claims "they don’t know how to".

"They want to make a deal, but they don’t know how to,"  he said during a campaign rally in Ohio. 

Trump added that Washington could not allow Tehran to acquire a nuclear weapon, describing the country as "the number one state sponsor of terror".

"Right now, they have no navy, they have no air force, they have no anti-aircraft, they have the worst inflation of any country anywhere in the world, they have no money," the US president said.

items.title: Who are Yemen's Houthis and what do they want?
items.summary_raw:
Who are Yemen's Houthis and what do they want?

Officially known as Ansar Allah, or "helpers of God", the movement emerged in Yemen's far north in the 1990s around the cleric Hussein al-Houthi.

It is rooted in Zaydism, a branch of Shia Islam whose followers are a minority in Yemen but concentrated in the northern highlands.

The group fought six rounds of war with the government of former president Ali Abdullah Saleh between 2004 and 2010. Hussein al-Houthi was killed in the first and leadership passed to his brother, Abdul-Malik al-Houthi, who still heads the movement.
